articles.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 gets a September release date
articles.summary: Microsoft shared new information about Minecraft Dungeons 2.
articles.body: Minecraft Dungeons 2, a sequel to Microsoft’s dungeon crawler spinoff Minecraft Dungeons, will be released on September 29th. The company originally revealed the game in a brief trailer in March, promising a fall 2026 release window. Here’s how Microsoft described it at the time: > Return to the world of Minecraft Dungeons in an all new action RPG adventure, brimming with high stakes encounters, thrilling challenges, and never before seen locations, as you set out to save a world in crisis. Will you and your allies prevail against the forces of evil and save the day once more? Minecraft Dungeons 2 will be available on Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S. The original Minecraft Dungeons launched in 2020, with my colleague Andrew Webster calling it a “lighter, more family-friendly take on Diablo.” There’s no mining or crafting in the game; instead, you tackle dungeons and loot cool gear.

articles.title: 'Gaming pays me double what I earned as a teacher'
articles.summary: Jarvs Tasker says it would have taken her 20 years as a teacher to make what she earns now.
articles.body:
In 2019, Jarvs Tasker was forced to give up her teaching career due to chronic illness when she was just 28.

Fast forward seven years, and she earns double her former annual salary, running Jarvs Indie Insights, which provides communication and marketing within the gaming industry.

She visited the University of Suffolk's e-sport building in Ipswich to celebrate independent game developers and studios on Wednesday.

"I can comfortably say it probably would have taken me about 20 years in teaching to earn what I make now," she said.

When Tasker left teaching, she initially started volunteering for PlayStation's YouTube channel, but she said there was lots of crossover between the two industries.

"Managing a community is very similar to managing a class of kids, so there's a lot of crossover skills there, but actually, video games is one of those industries where a lot of people come into it later on in life."

Tasker, who lives in Exeter, believed young people might not know the "many pathways" available in the industry.

"The video games community is very strong, and they will champion people that love what they do, but they'll also notice if you're in it just for the money," she continued.

Asked about the impact of AI, she said she believed the industry was doing a "really great job" at rejecting it, because players hated it.

"I think as an industry we should be really proud of the fact that we're still championing human creativity and that the audience is also on board with that," she added.

Tasker had been in Suffolk as part of an event hosted by Game Anglia to showcase the growing independent gaming industry in the East of England.

Mark Backler from Game Anglia said the industry was now one of the biggest in the UK , and while he agreed it was competitive, it was "more possible than ever to develop and release your own independent games".

"It's like being a content creator - it's tricky to be one of the standout ones, but it is doable," he said.

He added it was difficult to tell how AI would change things, but a lot of players were against its use.

Sam Read-Graves is a developer at Read Graves and works specifically in the East.

At the event, he said the gaming industry had "grown massively in the past 10 years".

"Because of schemes like Game Anglia across Suffolk, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk, there are really great clusters of a lot of students and a lot of developers, and I like to think that this has started to bring in studios who could make the big games.

"When it comes to those games like Call of Duty or FIFA, those at the minute aren't going to come out of the East of England because we don't have big studios.

"But when it comes to independent developers, there's no reason those games can't financially be as big."

Abbygale Dunn, 22, is the founder and director of Astral Forge, an independent game development company based in Essex.

She said there was "so much space for women" in the industry today.

"It's obviously daunting. When I studied, there were only about three women in my course," she said.

"Everyone is so kind; it's really not as bad as it seems, especially nowadays.

"As a programmer myself, which is more rare for women to be in, I've never felt out of place."

Omar Khalil is game scout lead at Entity and said there was "no shortage of talent in the UK", but it was challenging to create the next big game.

"There are so many games out there right now, and it's not like there aren't enough good games; it's how do you get visibility on those games?" he explained.

Additional reporting by Alice Cunningham.

articles.title: Corsair Gaming Headsets See Early Prime Big Deal Days Discounts on Amazon UK
articles.summary: Save early on Corsair gaming headsets at Amazon UK ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, featuring wireless VOID v2 and wired HS65 SURROUND models.
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially kick off until October 6, but we're already seeing some early discounts ahead of the two-day event, including savings on a couple of Corsair's gaming headsets.

Right now, you can pick up the Corsair VOID v2 wireless headset for £69.99 or the wired Corsair HS65 SURROUND for £72.78 at Amazon UK. Neither deal is officially part of Prime Big Deal Days yet, but if you've been looking for a new gaming headset, they're worth checking out before the main event gets underway.

Let's start with the Corsair VOID v2 , which is down to £69.99 at Amazon UK, a 30% saving.

It's a wireless headset with Corsair's distinctive styling, complete with lighting on the earcups, but there's more to it than looking the part. The VOID v2 packs Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio and custom-tuned 50mm drivers, designed to give you a better sense of where sounds are coming from in games.

That could mean picking up on a stealthy killer creeping around in Dead by Daylight , hearing where a grenade has landed in Battlefield 6 , or keeping track of proximity chat in ARC Raiders and Marathon .

Connectivity is another big selling point. The VOID v2 uses a 2.4GHz wireless dongle and Bluetooth, with support across PC, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch and mobile. You can switch between devices at the press of a button, which makes it a handy option if your gaming setup involves more than one platform.

Battery life is pretty impressive, too, with up to 70 hours of use on a full charge. Corsair says a quick 15-minute charge can also give you another six hours of playtime, which should be enough to get you through a particularly long gaming session.

If you'd rather keep things simple, the Corsair HS65 SURROUND is a wired alternative that's currently £72.78 at Amazon UK.

The benefit of a wired headset is that there's no battery to worry about, and the HS65 SURROUND can be plugged straight into compatible devices, including PS5, where it works with Sony's Tempest 3D AudioTech.

It also supports Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio and comes with memory foam earcups covered in leatherette, giving it a more premium feel than you might expect from a wired headset.

The microphone has flip-to-mute functionality, too, so you can quickly silence yourself without having to reach for a button when you're playing a game with proximity chat. That's particularly handy when you're trying not to accidentally broadcast whatever's happening in the room around you to everyone else in the lobby.

So, you've got a wireless headset with multi-platform connectivity and long battery life in the VOID v2, or a cheaper wired option in the HS65 SURROUND that doesn't need charging at all.

And while these aren't Prime Big Deal Days prices just yet, Amazon's main October sale is only around the corner. Prime Big Deal Days runs October 6-7 , so there's always a chance we'll see further reductions once the event officially begins.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Don't Breathe 3 in the Works With Stephen Lang and Jane Levy, Fede Álvarez Says
articles.summary: Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.
articles.body:
Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.

The filmmaker behind some of the grislier horror movies of the last 15 years announced his intentions to finish his thriller trilogy with a proper third film at Beyond Fest 2026, as reported by Dread Central . Whether or not Álvarez will return as director is unclear, but it is said that he has at least returned to handle its script.

How the third Don't Breathe movie will materialize and what story it will tell remains unclear. However, it sounds like it will at least continue where the previous two films left off, with both Stephen Lang (Avatar) and Jane Levy (Evil Dead) expected to reprise their roles as The Blind Man a.k.a. Norman Nordstrom and Rocky, respectively.

Álvarez and Levy previously worked together on his 2013 Evil Dead reboot before re-teaming for the original Don't Breathe in 2016. The horror-thriller, which was also produced by scary movie visionary Sam Raimi , follows three thieves who break into a house before finding themselves fighting for their lives in a "lethal game of cat and mouse."

Don't Breathe 2 continued the story with Lang back as The Blind Man in 2021. The sequel saw Álvarez hand directing duties to frequent collaborator Rodo Sayagues, with Raimi also returning as producer. In the five years since its premiere, there have been few updates about how the crew might round out the trilogy with a Don't Breathe 3 despite Lang teasing a new movie through the years .

After diverting his attention to direct Alien: Romulus in 2024, Álvarez seems more ready than ever to round out the story. How far along he is in that process is unclear, though, so we'll have to wait to learn more about its release date or who else may be attached.

Álvarez has also reportedly been in the mix to produce an Alien: Romulus sequel , but its status is unclear . As the filmmaker continues to try to expand upon the Don't Breathe universe, you can read IGN's 8.8/10 review of the first film and our 5/10 review of the second.

articles.title: Netflix Tried to Bring Obsession Straight to Streaming Before It Exploded in Theaters
articles.summary: Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.
articles.body:
Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.

The comedian-turned-horror-filmmaker talked about the early days of his record-breaking low-budget flick during a conversation on Q with Tom Power . We all know how Obsession turned out, but Barker said offers for the project nearly kept it out of theaters for a very different life as a streaming exclusive.

Barker said an early screening almost immediately resulted in "everybody" putting in offers to distribute Obsession. Neon, Focus, A24, and more wanted to bring Barker's twisted monkey's paw tale under their banner. Focus eventually won the war, but not before Netflix offered to throw a wrench into things.

"All of these companies are wanting to do your movie," Barker recalled hearing from his manager. "At this time, I'm still thinking maybe small theatrical release. Maybe they just want to acquire it, and also, as a director, I'm thinking, I'm scared of, 'Are they going to want to change my movie? Are they going to want to take out certain parts that I like?'

"So many questions were being thrown around. I think Netflix was in the conversation at one point. They put in an offer to just put it straight on Netflix. All of these conversations started."

With the odd exception , Netflix has infamously strayed from theatrical releases in the past. Before Paramount swooped in to acquire Warner Bros., the streaming giant was reportedly only interested in keeping its new slate of films in theaters for a little more than two weeks . Its movie boss, Dan Lin, said in June that the company "just won't work with" filmmakers who push to bring their films to theaters .

All signs point to a streaming-exclusive release for Obsession should Barker have signed with Netflix – but we all know that's not what happened. Instead, audiences spent months swarming movie theaters to see how stars Inde Navarrette, Michael Johnston, Cooper Tomlinson, and Megan Lawless helped bring the director's vision to life. It brought home massive early returns at the box office on its notably low $750,000 budget and then continued to surprise before reaching an unbelievable global total of $519.4 million (via Box Office Mojo ).

It was an unprecedented run that almost didn't happen if Netflix had proved victorious. There's no telling if Obsession would have had the same impact if it remained available to stream from the start, but Barker and company are probably happy enough with how things turned out. Although he and Tomlinson are still working on getting their next feature, Anything But Ghosts, ready for release, the director does have some ideas for a sequel in mind, even if it will be a while before Obsession 2 gets off the ground .

For more, you can read what Barker had to say about Gen Z's opinions on "slop" in movies . You can also check out how Universal brought Navarrette's Nikki to Halloween Horror Nights and then see IGN's top-reviewed horror movies of the year . Obsession, for example, earned an 8/10 .
